observacao: Carlos 'El Pibe' Valderrama is the greatest passer in Colombian football history and the all-time most-capped national team player. His vision and set-piece delivery set the standard for the AM/MID pool, justifying a near-perfect passing and dribbling percentile despite modest pace and physicality typical of a deep-lying creator.

Willington Ortiz was one of Colombia's most dazzling wingers of the 1970s and early 1980s, prized for explosive pace and dribbling that regularly beat defenders one-on-one. He sits in the long-time international starter band given sustained high performance across the 1975-1983 Copa America cycles, though pre-video-era records limit precision on his raw numbers.

Miguel Angel Borja is a modern-era target man known for strong hold-up play and clinical finishing at River Plate, a profile reflected in above-median shooting and physicality. He fits the solid international / squad regular tier rather than the all-time elite band, as his national team role has been that of a reliable scorer rather than a generational star.

Jackson Martinez was one of the most feared Colombian forwards of the 2010s, finishing as a top scorer in the Portuguese league with Porto before a high-profile move to China. His combination of pace, finishing, and physical presence places him in the long-time international starter of high level tier.

Teofilo Gutierrez combined flair and goal-scoring instinct during a successful spell at River Plate and regular Colombia call-ups, placing him in the solid international / squad regular tier with strong shooting and dribbling percentiles. His defensive contribution remains minimal, consistent with a creative forward profile.

Faustino Asprilla is a Colombian football legend, famous for his explosive, unpredictable style for Parma and Newcastle United and for his starring role in Colombia's golden generation of the 1990s. His blend of pace, dribbling, and finishing earns him a near all-time-great percentile within the ATT pool.

Victor Hugo Aristizabal is one of the most prolific goalscorers in Colombian football history, a long-time top scorer for Atletico Nacional and a consistent national team forward through multiple cycles. His shooting percentile sits near the top of the ATT pool, reflecting a career defined above all by finishing.

Antony 'El Pitufo' de Avila was a diminutive but extraordinarily skilled forward for America de Cali, celebrated for dribbling ability that made him one of Colombian football's most beloved figures. His percentile profile favors elite dribbling and finishing over physicality, consistent with his small stature and technical style.

Arnoldo Iguaran was a reliable forward for Millonarios during a pre-modern era of Colombian football with scarce statistical documentation. He is placed in the fringe / scarce-records tier, reflecting solid but not legendary national team involvement based on available sources.

Juan Pablo Angel enjoyed a long, prolific career at Aston Villa and River Plate, becoming one of the most reliable Colombian goalscorers of his generation at the highest European level. His finishing and physical presence place him firmly among long-time international starters of high level.

Adolfo Valencia was a powerful, physically dominant striker who won the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich and was a mainstay of Colombia's national team through the 1990s. His physicality and shooting percentiles rank near the top of the ATT pool, reflecting a battering-ram forward style.

Leonel Alvarez was a key defensive midfield anchor for Colombia's celebrated 1990 World Cup squad, combining disciplined defending with reliable distribution. His percentile profile reflects a long-time international starter whose value lay in ball-winning and physical control of the midfield.

Freddy Rincon is one of Colombia's greatest-ever midfielders, remembered for powerful box-to-box play, a famous World Cup goal against West Germany in 1990, and a spell at Real Madrid. His well-rounded, elite profile across passing, shooting, and physicality places him near the top of the national-legend band.

Wilmar Barrios has been a combative defensive midfielder for Boca Juniors and a consistent Colombia national team starter in the 2018-2024 cycles. His strong defending and physical percentiles reflect a disciplined destroyer role in front of the back line.

Ivan Cordoba was an elite central defender and long-time captain of Inter Milan, bringing exceptional pace and defensive reading to one of Europe's top clubs across more than a decade. He ranks among the long-time international starters of high level with elite defending and physicality.

Mario Yepes captained Colombia to the 2014 World Cup quarter-finals after a distinguished European career including a spell at AC Milan, establishing himself as one of the country's greatest central defenders. His near-elite defending and physical percentiles reflect that leadership and longevity.

Alexis Garcia was a squad member of Colombia's 1990 World Cup campaign, contributing steady midfield play without the standout statistical record of the era's biggest stars. He is placed in the solid squad regular tier given scarce pre-modern records.

Camilo Zuniga was a fast, attacking-minded right-back who starred for Napoli and was a key piece of Colombia's 2014 World Cup quarter-final run. His pace and defending percentiles rank well above the DEF pool median, consistent with a modern attacking full-back profile.

Pablo Armero was an energetic attacking left-back for Udinese and a fixture of Colombia's 2014 World Cup squad, prized for overlapping runs and pace down the flank. His high pace percentile reflects that attacking profile while defending remains solid but secondary.

Carlos Sanchez was a dependable defensive midfielder during his time at Aston Villa and a regular Colombia international through the 2010s, valued for positional discipline and tenacity. His defending and physical percentiles place him comfortably in the solid international tier.

Abel Aguilar was a consistent defensive and box-to-box midfielder for Colombia through multiple World Cup and Copa America cycles, including a spell at Toulouse in France. His balanced percentile profile fits the squad regular tier of long-serving international midfielders.

Fabian Vargas was a technically sound central midfielder who played for Boca Juniors and represented Colombia across the 2000s, contributing steady passing and ball progression. His profile sits in the solid international / squad regular tier.

Giovanny Hernandez was a creative attacking midfielder for Deportivo Cali with intermittent national team involvement and comparatively scarce international records. He is placed in the fringe tier, reflecting solid domestic quality without extensive documented national team impact.

Luis Amaranto Perea was a physically imposing, rugged central defender who played for Atletico Madrid and anchored the Colombia national team backline for years. His elite defending and physical percentiles reflect a long-time international starter of high level.

Jorge Bermudez was a tough, commanding central defender and club legend at Boca Juniors who represented Colombia across multiple World Cup cycles. His strong defending and physicality percentiles place him among solid long-time international starters.

Mauricio Serna was a tenacious defensive midfielder who won multiple titles with Boca Juniors and represented Colombia across several World Cup and Copa America cycles. His strong defending and physical percentiles reflect a reliable, long-serving midfield anchor.

Faryd Mondragon is a Colombian goalkeeping legend whose international career spanned an extraordinary two decades, from 1994 to 2014, making him the oldest player to appear at a World Cup at the time. His near-elite percentiles across all goalkeeping attributes reflect that remarkable longevity at the highest level.

Oscar Cordoba was Colombia's long-time starting goalkeeper through the 1990s and early 2000s and a title-winning club legend at Boca Juniors. His consistently high goalkeeping percentiles reflect sustained elite performance as a long-time international starter.

Rene 'El Loco' Higuita revolutionized the sweeper-keeper role in world football, famous for his ball-playing ability, aggressive positioning far from goal, and the iconic scorpion kick save. His exceptional kicking and speed percentiles reflect that unconventional, trailblazing style among the all-time great Colombia goalkeepers.
